structured.answer: The page says to hold it at פסגות and buy "אי.בי.אי. מחקה (4A) ת"א 125" (number 5112628), and with 10,000 ₪ now plus 500 ₪ a month you'd have about 86,045 ₪ after ten years. But I don't really understand what I'd be buying, the minus signs worry me, and I'd call you before I did anything.

stuck.why: A dark page with English letters (MSCI, S&P 500, נאסד"ק). It nearly felt not for me, but ת"א-125 was already picked, so I stayed.
The '−1,030 ₪' minus made me back away from that one, and I didn't understand what a 'זוג' is.
'−0.04%' with 'בשנה · שנה אחת'. Does that mean the fund I'm meant to choose lost money? It frightened me.
A long list full of numbers and coloured bars. I got tired and anxious.

findings.what: Minus signs ('−0.04%', '−1,030 ₪') right next to the recommended fund, with no explanation. It looks like losing money.
It opens with English index names on a dark background, which makes it feel not for people like me.
The 86,045 ₪ depends on a 7% a year return I never chose, and the page doesn't clearly say this could come out differently or lower.
Long list of banks with many numbers and coloured bars is tiring and hard to follow.
The cost bar colours (orange and yellow, red and pink) are close together and hard to tell apart.
Lots of jargon: קרן מחקה, נאמן, דמי משמרת, הזוג.
I don't know who 'מקור' is, so I'm not sure I can trust the advice.
